overall_note: Risk-weighted guess with a wide error bar. The page prefers the live figure in `docs/status.md` when it can read one.
machine: 14-inch MacBook Pro, M2 Pro (`T6020`, `apple,j414s`), Aurora Silicon Linux

goal.linux_night: 23% of the battery a night, about 1.7 days from full with the lid closed
goal.macos_night: 5.9 h lid closed on battery, 98.7% of it in S2R

phases.name: Remote hands
phases.short: Recovery without anyone at the Mac
phases.summary: The USB-PD board and smart plug were dropped (no extra hardware). Recovery comes from software instead, and it is proven.
done: Aura arms the hardware watchdog (WD1, 120 s) around `SYSTEM_SUSPEND`; a deliberate hang (image 27-hang) reset the Mac by itself
Every test image boots once; an early unit puts the default `boot.bin` back and checks its sha
Wi-Fi guard reboots a boot that never connects, with a 3-strike limit
The Raspberry Pi 5 streams the kernel log off the machine during risky runs
next: A sleep that never wakes in full S2R still needs the owner at the power key
phases.gate: Unattended runs recover from a hang without hands.

phases.name: CPU_ON and CPU_OFF
phases.summary: PSCI-via-EFI is built in the kernel, Aura and U-Boot. CPU_ON brings all nine secondaries up. CPU_OFF followed by CPU_ON still hangs the SoC, and testing is paused because the hard resets lost the NVMe's cached writes.
done: Kernel: the PSCI-via-EFI RFC's six patches plus `t6020-j414s-psci.dts`
Aura: `psci.c`, `smp_psci_*`, `dt_set_psci()`; U-Boot: `efi_platform_register()`
CPU_ON of cpu1 to cpu9 in 0.25 s, also from a RAM-only boot that never touches the root filesystem
Found why RAM-only logs vanished: the ANS firmware caches writes until a clean `saveCtx` shutdown
next: Park the core with a plain WFI instead of deep WFI, one change per image
Read-only root and the Pi’s kmsg stream, with the owner’s yes
phases.gate: Each secondary offline and online 100 times, deep idle not worse, RVBAR re-entry works.

phases.name: SYSTEM_SUSPEND, SoC on
phases.short: Linux’s full suspend path with a firmware that hands back
phases.summary: `mem_sleep` offers `deep`. On the boot CPU alone (`maxcpus=1`) the whole Linux suspend and resume path runs, and Aura sleeps the core in deep WFI until a real wake source fires.
done: 20 of 20 suspend/resume cycles with Aura’s fixed wait (image 16), after a kernel fix for the EFI virtmap unwind
Wakes on the PMU RTC alarm (3 of 3, about 11 s for a 10 s alarm)
Wakes on the power key through the SMC mailbox line 865
Works with the PMP running, and through `systemctl suspend` with the sleep hooks
Deep WFI with state retention on the boot core (image 31)
next: Image 37: the 20-cycle gate with deep WFI and the RVBAR backstop
Lid wake, not tested separately yet
Multi-CPU suspend, which needs Phase 1’s hotplug
phases.gate: 20 of 20 cycles back in Linux with no device errors.

phases.name: Trace macOS sleeping
phases.summary: The guest boots under the hypervisor with all 10 CPUs and the SMC and PMP tracers. Runs 7 to 11 captured macOS’s sleep entry in order. The wake is not visible under the hypervisor, so the raw-boot-mode risk is still open.
done: `macOSTest` volume (14.8.9; 14.8.3 is gone from Apple’s catalog) with Aura as its boot object
Three Aura and tracer fixes (`patches/hvsleep-trace`)
The ordered sleep entry: `slpw`, the PMP display power-down, `slpa`, `SetAPPower` 0x201, the CPU complexes off, deep WFI on every core
next: Find what restarts the AP on wake, and through which RVBAR
Answer whether iBoot arms the wake path for a raw image
phases.gate: An ordered list of every sleep and wake write, and a macOS wake under the hypervisor.

phases.name: Devices survive power loss
phases.summary: Each device has to come back after its power is really removed. The SMC handshake is mapped and NVMe already survives Phase 2’s suspends. The PMP wake is unsolved, and DCP is the long pole.
done: SMC: `WKTP` and `slpw` are harmless; `slpa` takes the storage away, so it goes last
PMP: RTKit IDLE acks in about 400 us
NVMe: `saveCtx` shutdown and resume, every Phase 2 cycle
next: PMP: macOS’s DART off/on and outbox steps around RUN, no reset
PCIe L2 entry and D3cold resume (no remove/rescan)
DCP: full shutdown and restart of its firmware
phases.gate: Each device passes 20 cycles with its power actually removed.

phases.name: Full S2R
phases.short: The SoC powers down, DRAM in self-refresh
phases.summary: Aura’s `SYSTEM_SUSPEND` gains the SoC steps in macOS’s order: PMGR quiesce, the S2R timer, the PMU SPMI quiesce and `slpa`, then `restoreHW` on wake.
done: The PMGR, SMC and PMP sleep actions read from the macOS 13.5 kernelcache
next: First cycle with the PMU alarm as the only wake and the owner at the power key
phases.gate: 20 of 20 cycles; lid, key, keyboard and alarm wakes; about 0.3 W on battery.

phases.name: Daily use
phases.summary: U-Boot passes Aura’s PSCI table on, Omarchy’s suspend uses `deep`, and the patches go to Aurora’s trees.

pieces.name: Timed wake
pieces.known: The PMU RTC alarm on SPMI irq 2, AIC 724. The “fired” bit must be cleared before re-arming. Upstream’s alarm is T6030-only, so the T602x patches are still needed.
pieces.next: Shape it for upstream; power-on from off is untested

pieces.name: Boot CPU hand-back
pieces.known: `SYSTEM_SUSPEND` returns through the kernel’s `cpu_resume`, 20 of 20. With retention the core sleeps and comes back. Powered down without retention, it never re-enters at RVBAR (images 32 to 36).
pieces.next: Full S2R wakes through a different route

pieces.name: Wake sources
pieces.known: Deep WFI with AIC lines 724 (alarm) and 865 (SMC mailbox) unmasked. The power key wakes on 865.
pieces.next: Lid; stop the SMC’s early `Elec Cause` syslog wakes

pieces.name: AIC
pieces.known: Save and mask every bank, restore on resume (syscore). It runs on every Phase 2 cycle. Because it masks everything, wake detection has to come from the PMU/SMC side.

pieces.name: SMC handshake
pieces.known: `WKTP` and `slpw` are harmless. `slpa` makes NVMe I/O fail after resume and outlasts a warm reboot. `SetAPPower` IDLE is acked and safe.
pieces.next: `slpa` last, on the real path only

pieces.name: PMP
pieces.known: IDLE works. RUN alone woke it 0 of 3. Gating `ps_pms_sram` does not restart it, and a PMGR reset of `ps_pmp` crashes the SoC.
pieces.next: DART off/on and outbox steps around RUN

pieces.name: Secondary CPUs
pieces.known: CPU_ON works for all nine. CPU_OFF then CPU_ON hangs the SoC.

pieces.name: PMGR quiesce, S2R timer
pieces.known: Read statically from macOS 13.5. The last write goes to an always-on PMGR block Linux does not map.
pieces.next: The wake half of the trace

pieces.name: Devices
pieces.known: s2idle only. DCP cannot resume from power loss today.

findings.title: The gap is SoC sleep itself
findings.body: Awake idle matches macOS once the PMP runs (5.38 W against 5.57 W, SoC 1.22 W on both). The lid-closed gap is not the devices.

findings.title: s2idle’s 1.4 W is power left on, not wakes
findings.body: The 3.2 wakes a second come from the AOP’s ambient-light and lid-angle reports and cost milliwatts. The PMP doesn’t change the drain.

findings.title: macOS tells the PMP when the system sleeps
findings.body: Read from the macOS 13.5 kernelcache: the full order of sleep and quiesce actions, the SMC `MBSE` handshake, PMGR’s last write, and the PMP’s RTKit IDLE (0x201), which is Linux’s unused `apple_rtkit_idle()`.

findings.title: `slpa` takes the storage away
findings.body: After `slpa` in s2idle every NVMe access failed, and the state survived a warm reboot. It means the SoC is about to lose power, so it belongs last.

findings.title: The PMP’s wake from IDLE is a power cycle
findings.body: RUN alone woke it 0 of 3. Gating its SRAM did not restart it, and resetting `ps_pmp` crashed the SoC. `ps_pmp` is pinned on by iBoot.

findings.title: ISR_EL1 is blind at EL2 under VHE
findings.body: With IMO/FMO set, Aura saw only the virtual pending state. The fix was to watch the AIC’s HW_STATE for the alarm line.

findings.title: The kernel masks the whole AIC for suspend
findings.body: `aic_syscore_suspend` masks every line, as macOS does. In real S2R the wake must be detected from the PMU/SMC side.

findings.title: A core powered down without retention doesn’t come back on an IRQ
findings.body: Across images 32 to 36 the boot core never re-entered at RVBAR. Secondaries only return through a PMGR CPU-start written by another core.

findings.title: NVMe drops cached writes on a hard reset
findings.body: The ANS firmware caches until a clean `saveCtx` shutdown. That explained the lost logs and the filesystem damage after hotplug hangs.

findings.title: The PMU RTC alarm is the timed wake
findings.body: Linux had no driver for the alarm macOS uses for dark wakes. `rtcwake -m freeze -s 30` woke after about 31 s, 3 of 3.

rules: Never remove and rescan PCI devices: it kills Wi-Fi until a reboot.
No `slpa` without the owner at the power key and the Pi watcher on.
Keep a `.keep` file in module trees pacman doesn’t own.
No hotplug tests on a boot that can hurt the root filesystem.
Check the ESP sha after every copy, and refuse to suspend on the default image.
unknowns: Whether iBoot arms the wake path (reconfig engine, boot CPU RVBAR) for a raw image as it does for a kernelcache.
What restarts the AP on wake in macOS, and through which RVBAR.
What the reconfig engine runs on `SLP_S2R`, and what each quiesce action writes.
Why CPU_OFF followed by CPU_ON hangs the SoC.
Whether a DCP with nothing attached can be shut down and restarted.
What the PMP’s VLPM tunables control.
